contracts.claim: An authenticated bond session can repair lanes indefinitely without exhausting admission state or weakening replay rejection.

The window must cover every concurrently prepared admission, accept bounded out-of-order completion, and reject duplicate or older captured joins. Legacy v1/v2 peers retain their bounded random-nonce ledger because silently evicting those nonces would make an old authenticated hello replayable. The 2026-10-12 generation-9 endurance run added 976 phases in one session, reached sequence 1265, crossed both former exhaustion boundaries, and completed cleanly after 24 hours.

Deterministic admission tests accept more than 256 sequential current-version repairs in one session with constant replay state, accept unseen out-of-order joins inside the window, reject duplicate and stale sequences, and preserve the bounded legacy nonce limit. A retained-state endurance run then crosses both the prior stream-127 boundary and the observed 256-join failure boundary without session loss.

contracts.claim: Every product slot starts and repairs independently, so a slow provider attempt cannot block unrelated topology progress or disrupt other sessions.

contracts.exit_condition: A packaged fixed-cardinality campaign covers 1+1, 2+2, 4+4, and 8+8 over one bounded campaign-local persistent router corpus; stops router processes between trials; gives each topology repeated small client-to-server, larger server-to-client, and sustained simultaneous bidirectional exact transfers; begins real-time requests during bulk and retains their complete latency even when a slow echo outlives a short transfer; and records raw per-round aggregate goodput and real-time latency together with directional hashes, runtime-derived protected and bulk-eligible paths, router-state age, startup duration, CPU, RSS, disk footprint, maximum lane queue delay, whole-trial and formation-specific retransmissions, liveness failures, control replays, inactive-lane observations, repair cycles, and Tor/I2P acknowledgement contribution. Deterministic supervision proves fixed mode latches full demand without changing the adaptive default; authenticated runtime tests prove distinct simultaneous directional streams; and always-ready and deliberately blocked writer proofs show paced formation pressure cannot monopolize its async task or miss cancellation while flow-controlled.

contracts.claim: An authenticated bond session remains alive and applies bounded backpressure when every current lane is temporarily unavailable, then resumes exact delivery when an independently supervised lane returns.
contracts.assumption: The authenticated session state, send ledger, receive state, declared topology, and pending authenticated topology control remain in memory while no lane is active; lane supervisors retain bounded retry and authentication requirements. Explicit session close and unrecoverable protocol violations remain terminal.
contracts.exit_condition: A deterministic full-duplex runtime proof fails the sole active lane with payload and a topology advertisement outstanding, observes a live zero-lane session rather than actor termination, authenticates a replacement lane, retransmits stranded payload exactly once, flushes deferred acknowledgement, window, and topology state, and completes clean stream and session shutdown. The packaged public-overlay recovery campaign survives that formation race, then restores all sixteen adaptive-load lanes and one retained-state slot from each provider with exact delivery and zero unacknowledged bytes.

contracts.claim: Every public session operation that observes an internally terminated runtime reports the recorded terminal cause instead of collapsing it to an unqualified stopped error.
contracts.assumption: The first terminal runtime error is authoritative diagnostic state; exposing its bounded display string does not disclose payload, key, endpoint, or identity material.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests force an authenticated runtime protocol failure and prove blocked topology, stream acceptance, and stream reads wake with the original terminal cause; existing-stream write and close, new-stream creation, and session shutdown preserve the same cause without nested generic wrappers. Recovery and scaling campaign error JSON serializes the complete bounded cause chain.

contracts.claim: A managed router that exits or exceeds its startup deadline reports enough bounded diagnostic context to distinguish process, configuration, endpoint, and network-bootstrap failures.
contracts.assumption: Router stdout and stderr are drained continuously into a fixed-size in-memory tail, never persisted as unbounded router logs, and long token-like material plus network endpoints are redacted before a failure enters a public error or test artifact.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests prove output capture retains only the configured tail, redacts bare, prefixed, bracketed, IPv4, IPv6, and scheme-qualified endpoints plus padded identity material, strips terminal escapes, and preserves useful failure text. Managed i2pd and Tor exit and deadline paths use the same sanitized diagnostic builder, while successful operation retains no output files.

contracts.claim: Every internally allocated Tor SOCKS/control or I2P SAM endpoint remains exclusively owned by its managed router slot across deferred startup, failure backoff, stop, and repair.
contracts.assumption: Discovering a free anonymous port and retaining only its number is a time-of-check/time-of-use race: another listener in the same process can claim it before a deferred router starts. A configured unoccupied endpoint is owned by its manager immediately; an occupied I2P SAM endpoint remains eligible only as an explicitly health-checked external router, while occupied Tor endpoints fail closed because their control authentication is unavailable.
contracts.exit_condition: Managed-router constructors either consume bound loopback reservations or reserve available configured endpoints, retain them through configuration work, release them only immediately before child spawn, and reclaim them before repair and whenever the child is absent. Deterministic tests prove unrelated listeners cannot steal deferred, repeatedly failed, repaired, or stopped I2P or Tor endpoints, occupied Tor endpoints fail closed without leaking partial reservations, and an occupied I2P endpoint is used only after a valid SAM exchange. Product and live pool constructors consume the same reservation type without a separate anonymous-port convention.

contracts.claim: The shipped doctor describes and validates the complete default bonded router topology before a user starts a server or connection.
contracts.assumption: Configuration diagnosis must not start routers, claim configured ports, require an identity password, or mistake an intentionally stopped persistent router for a broken installation. It validates static topology separately from optional live endpoint probes.
contracts.exit_condition: Doctor JSON reports the 8 Tor slots, 16 Tor candidates, 8 I2P slots, mixed 2+2 baseline lane IDs, every persistent state root, and every configured loopback endpoint; deterministic tests require unique roots, unique provider-role endpoints, expected cardinalities, and a fail-closed invalid detail when configured endpoints collide or leave loopback. Packaged smoke captures a valid topology report.

contracts.claim: An active bulk lane cannot be permanently starved by an obsolete delivery estimate; it receives bounded periodic traffic evidence while useful capacity remains scheduled by predicted delivery time.
contracts.assumption: Forcing equal provider shares would reduce aggregate performance and amplify reassembly head-of-line delay, but probing only at activation cannot discover a path that later improves. A small per-lane probe budget on a fixed monotonic interval bounds exploration cost while preserving automatic recovery of useful Tor or I2P capacity.
contracts.exit_condition: The allocation-free scheduler gives every eligible lane one bounded probe budget on activation, restoration, and each elapsed reprobe interval; protected lanes remain bulk-clean while alternatives exist; between intervals normal predicted-delivery scheduling may exclude a slower lane; deterministic tests prove expiry, bounded overhead, and restoration behavior; the live scale campaign starts measured traffic after a fresh interval and records acknowledged bytes on both providers without requiring equal shares.

contracts.claim: A failed lane cannot permanently discard authenticated cumulative control state and strand an otherwise repairable bonded stream or session.
contracts.assumption: A successful local queue operation does not prove that a control record reached the peer. Pending stream opens and closes, current absolute receive credit, completed remote-close acknowledgements, the newest cumulative topology snapshot, and an outstanding session-close request or acknowledgement are replayed after lane loss or replacement. Crossing session-close requests remain pending until each locally initiated request receives its authenticated acknowledgement; receiving the peer request does not permit aborting an unwritten local request. Exact authenticated duplicates are idempotent; a duplicate with conflicting class, initial window, final offset, or topology generation remains a protocol error.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests discard queued controls with their lane, retain at least one healthy lane or add a replacement, and prove exact stream open, flow-control continuation, acknowledged half-close, topology delivery, and clean session shutdown. Duplicate open and close controls produce one application event and matching acknowledgements, while conflicting duplicates fail closed; runtime statistics count replayed controls.

contracts.claim: An installed resident broker adapts its warm local Tor and I2P substrate to the selected resource profile, recent destination demand, measured startup cost, and idle cost while the co-resident recovery server owns a disjoint router pool.
contracts.assumption: A target-specific authenticated bond cannot exist before a recovery descriptor and password-derived key are available. Readiness therefore means persistent local routers, not speculative remote sessions. Client and server roles must never share managed endpoints or state roots. Active physical-slot demand is authoritative and can never be stopped by the warm controller. Persistent router state is never deleted automatically; a state quota is an admission and health boundary, while only old content-addressed runtime cache entries are eligible for safe quota garbage collection.
contracts.exit_condition: Configuration v2 strictly validates external Tor declarations, resident limits, cache and state quotas, and old-runtime retention while retaining v0/v1 migration. Deterministic policy tests prove profile-specific floors and ceilings, immediate minimum-topology and global-demand ramp-up, startup-cost-aware idle retention, memory-pressure response, gradual contraction, session and connection limits, and refusal to drain physically demanded slots. Filesystem tests prove garbage collection remains beneath the private runtime cache, rejects symlinks, preserves current payloads and persistent router state, and enforces cache bounds. State quota tests prove established sessions remain reusable while new destinations fail closed. Broker status v7 reports the effective policy, warm target, and storage result. External Tor attachment is sourced from configuration rather than systemd environment drop-ins.

contracts.claim: Concurrent client commands for the same recovery identity reuse one authenticated bond session and one managed router pool through a resident per-user broker instead of competing for fixed endpoints and state roots.
contracts.assumption: One broker socket lives in a private per-user directory and owns the shared client router pool. Its bounded registry keys sessions by exact provider topology, compares the derived bond key in constant time before reuse, and removes stale sockets safely. On-demand brokers exit after a bounded idle interval; installed resident brokers do not. A wrong password cannot borrow an already unlocked topology.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic lease and registry tests prove exactly one socket owner, stale reclamation, topology separation, constant-time wrong-key rejection without allocating another session, bounded request codecs, and clean proxy termination. A packaged live process proof races two first `anonssh connect` commands, records one broker and router pool, rejects a same-topology wrong-key proxy, opens independent streams for held clients, bulk, typing, and a later warm reconnect without replacing the broker or remote bond session, then stops cleanly and leaves no test-owned process or socket.

contracts.claim: One authenticated product bond session can carry multiple independent SSH backend connections so bulk backlog on one ordered stream cannot block typing on another.
contracts.assumption: Each accepted Interactive BondedStream receives its own bounded backend relay and failure scope; topology control remains session-scoped; the stream and backend limits fail closed without terminating healthy sibling streams.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests concurrently open, relay, half-close, and independently fail multiple SSH-class streams while topology control continues. A packaged live test uploads a long exact payload on one ordinary client command while a second ordinary shell issues exact typing-sized commands over the same broker and bond session; it records distinct stream IDs, bounded typing p95, exact bulk hash, no cross-stream reset, and one shared router pool.

contracts.claim: Sustained demand can admit multiple useful candidate lanes per control interval and sustained quiet can retire multiple surplus lanes per interval, without waiting one fixed interval per lane, while short interactive bursts do not start the full router pool.
contracts.assumption: Parallel admission remains bounded by provider, CPU, memory, startup, and maximum-active budgets; authenticated topology snapshots can request a bounded batch atomically. Only queue-, window-, or application-pressure admissions are speculative: two pressure-free evaluations cancel every member that has not become active. Active marginal lanes retain observation and drain hysteresis before one bounded drain batch, which preserves minimum topology, provider diversity, required lanes, and protected low-latency capacity.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic controller tests prove bounded batch admission and retirement, provider-balanced ranking, topology floors, no expansion for typing-only bursts, cancellation when pressure clears, and faster convergence than one-action-per-ten-seconds without exceeding resource budgets. A packaged adaptive SSH artifact records demand-to-useful-capacity time, concurrent starts, exact transfer, typing latency, and contraction within its fixed deadline.

contracts.claim: Scaling policy is evaluated across cardinality, direction, payload duration, concurrent users, I2P state age, and churn rather than inferred from one 4+4/8+8 campaign.
contracts.assumption: Public-overlay results remain descriptive and same-host resource contention remains explicit; exact delivery, bounded latency, provider contribution, process cleanup, and machine-readable checkpoints are hard requirements. Fixed-cardinality transport scaling, real concurrent SSH clients, fresh-I2P recovery, adaptive controller actions, and destructive lane churn have different causal boundaries and therefore remain separate packaged artifacts in one evidence suite rather than being collapsed into one ambiguous score. Real-time evidence must issue requests at a fixed cadence independently of prior echo completion; otherwise severe tail latency censors later samples and can fail the observer instead of measuring the product.
contracts.exit_condition: The packaged checkpointed live-bond-scale campaign covers 1, 2, 4, and 8 lanes per provider with repeated exact rounds of short client-to-server, long server-to-client, and simultaneous bidirectional sustained bulk while typing requests begin under load and slow complete echoes remain evidence; labels fresh, partially retained, and retained router state; compares every adjacent cardinality; and reports startup, formation, goodput, typing percentiles, CPU, RSS, disk, queue delay, retransmission, liveness, per-provider contribution, and exact protected-pool use. Packaged companion artifacts prove multiple concurrent SSH clients and streams, reseed-disabled fresh I2P, adaptive controller expansion/contraction, and repeated Tor/I2P/zero-lane churn, each with exact delivery and complete process cleanup.

contracts.claim: AnonSSH can test a 16+16 mixed topology without changing the shipped 8+8 candidate pool or treating maximum cardinality as a performance goal.
contracts.assumption: A 32-lane experiment uses 64 same-host router processes and may consume several GiB of memory plus more than one GiB of transient state. It is therefore explicit, finite, checkpointed, self-cleaning, and excluded from normal gates. Raising the authenticated topology/runtime ceiling preserves the existing wire encoding, but release defaults remain at 16 total lanes until repeated marginal-goodput and latency evidence justifies a larger pool. The completed v7 soak found 16+16 useful only for simultaneous bidirectional traffic, where 1.70x median goodput over 8+8 cost roughly twice the RSS and disk; short and reverse median goodput regressed to 0.76x and 0.97x, so 32 lanes remain evidence-only.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests prove 32-descriptor topology round trips, reject descriptor 33, form stable 16+16 recovery identities that extend the locked 8+8 prefixes, exercise the runtime's 32-lane accounting bound, and prove fixed-cadence real-time probes are not serialized behind slow echoes. An explicit packaged soak campaign covers 1+1 through 16+16 in both directions and simultaneous bidirectional traffic with repeated exact hashes, real-time overlap, runtime-derived protected paths, per-provider contribution, resource telemetry, atomic checkpoints, and complete process/state cleanup.

contracts.claim: A packaged endurance campaign can keep a stable mixed-router corpus warm for an operator-selected duration, continuously challenge the production adaptive controller, and measure whether retained router age improves useful throughput or latency without accumulating unbounded test output.
contracts.assumption: Public-overlay results remain descriptive and same-host contention remains explicit. Persistent Tor and i2pd roots are the experimental subject and survive clean campaign exits; sessions, sockets, leases, and router processes do not. Sustained client-to-server and bidirectional phases create admission pressure, reverse phases expose directional asymmetry, and quiet real-time phases permit measured contraction. Active lanes retain the scheduler's bounded periodic exploration. A zero overall duration means operator-terminated rather than unbounded individual operations: a duration or signal request finishes the active exact phase, and every phase and cleanup still has a deadline. Evidence stores fixed cumulative aggregates, a bounded initial baseline, and a bounded rolling observation window rather than append-only logs; those bounded records survive later invocations with the same corpus and tag every observation with corpus generation and age. Cumulative lane counters alone are insufficient because a bounded rolling window can no longer reconstruct phase contribution after older observations are evicted, so every retained observation stores phase-local endpoint, provider, and lane deltas. Crossing the configured persistent-state ceiling fails closed and stops every owned process. The 2026-10-10 generation-7 run completed 289 phases over 4 hours 42 minutes but phase 290 exposed exhaustion of the former 256-nonce session admission ledger. After that defect was repaired, the 2026-10-12 generation-9 run completed the configured 24 hours, added 976 exact phases, reached sequence 1265, retained bounded history and state below the 2 GiB ceiling, and cleaned every owned process, socket, session, and lease.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests lock configuration bounds, workload cycling, stable state-generation metadata, bounded evidence retention, v1-to-v2 history migration, aggregate accounting, exact monotonic phase deltas, provider and maximum-lane contribution summaries, and atomic checkpoint replacement. The packaged target defaults to a 24-hour 16+16 candidate campaign, permits duration zero for SIGINT/SIGTERM operation, runs the real adaptive controller across repeated exact forward, bidirectional, reverse, and quiet real-time phases, and records state age, exact hashes, goodput, latency percentiles, adaptive generations, desired/active/protected lanes, per-lane phase delivery, provider contribution, maximum-lane share, endpoint-local frame/ACK/window/probe/retransmission/liveness/backpressure deltas, final live/tombstone/reorder/queue state, CPU, RSS, and bounded disk use. One retained-state run must cross both the previous stream-127 tombstone-horizon failure boundary and the observed 256-join admission boundary without session loss before the campaign can be promoted. Graceful duration or signal completion writes a final checkpoint only after both endpoint pools report zero owned router processes, removes the exclusive campaign lease, retains only the explicitly bounded router corpus, and can resume that corpus in a later run.

contracts.claim: Router and lane admission decisions account for the union of local sessions so independent clients cannot each spend the full endpoint CPU and memory budget or drain resources another session needs.
contracts.assumption: The resident client broker and persistent server ingress are the authority for endpoint-local process demand; per-session schedulers retain independent path measurements, while physical router admission and retirement use one shared reference-counted authority. A physical provider slot is charged once even when several logical sessions use it. Required baseline registration is atomic and a new session fails closed if its additional physical slots cannot fit; optional additions may be denied without terminating an established baseline. Protected active and standby lanes are contained in each admitted baseline. Conservative startup costs prevent concurrent admissions from racing past cardinality, CPU, or memory ceilings before process telemetry exists; observed process pressure can still cause later adaptive retirement.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic multi-session tests apply overlapping and disjoint mixed, Tor-only, and I2P-only demands; prove atomic baseline admission, shared-slot accounting, transactional optional add/replace/drain, aggregate cardinality/CPU/memory bounds, and rollback after a failed topology publication; preserve baseline/protected capacity for every admitted live session; and require a router-stop decision only after the final dependent session releases it. Broker status exports bounded aggregate governor state. The packaged `make live-concurrent-bond-ssh` v5 campaign authenticates three simultaneous SSH clients against two destinations, opens six session-qualified streams through one broker and router pool, hash-verifies 16 MiB while measuring an independent typing stream, and reports two logical sessions sharing exactly two Tor and two I2P processes under the low profile before complete cleanup.

contracts.claim: One endpoint-wide optimizer admits physical Tor and I2P paths from aggregate delivered value and measured machine cost instead of allowing each logical bond session to optimize against a separate estimated budget.
contracts.assumption: Per-session controllers continue to report application pressure and lane health, but the shared broker governor is the final authority for optional physical-slot admission. One router process is charged once even when several destination sessions use it; its CPU and RSS are conservatively aggregated from endpoint observations while delivered goodput and queue pressure aggregate across dependent sessions. Missing measurements retain conservative provider estimates. Required baselines are never displaced, and failed authenticated topology publication rolls back the tentative global reservation.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic multi-session tests prove that measured CPU/RSS can both admit a path that conservative estimates would reject and deny one whose live cost exceeds its estimate; shared paths remain charged once; aggregate useful goodput and pressure rank optional admissions independently of caller order; observations from removed sessions stop contributing; malformed, duplicate, zero-cost, and unknown-session reports fail closed; transactional rollback restores the prior global allocation; and broker status exports bounded measured-versus-estimated coverage and aggregate goodput.

contracts.claim: Adaptive topology control learns bounded per-path behavior and derives decisions from recent performance instead of treating one fixed queue, goodput, replacement, startup, and cadence policy as universally correct.
contracts.assumption: The fixed resource profile supplies safety ceilings, not a target cardinality: the mixed baseline remains 2+2, a homogeneous baseline remains four, performance mode permits at most sixteen total active lanes, and the product's 8+8 candidate inventory does not imply sixteen active lanes. The explicit 16+16 topology remains a stress/soak facility rather than a product default. Bounded exponentially weighted priors retain goodput, queue delay, startup, CPU, RSS, and confidence for each declared slot. Immediate backpressure accelerates observation and admission; scale-down requires the existing active dwell plus repeated quiet evidence; stale or unmeasured candidates receive bounded periodic exploration; no learner may weaken minimum topology, provider diversity, protected-lane, protocol, or resource constraints.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic virtual-time tests prove bounded priors, dynamic queue and marginal-goodput thresholds, confidence-sensitive replacement, learned startup ceilings, fast pressure cadence, slow quiet retirement, periodic exploration without unbounded cardinality, and utility-per-CPU/RSS ordering. Tests also prove that the sixteen-candidate mixed plan starts at four active lanes, can expand and contract within a sixteen-lane ceiling, retains Tor-only and I2P-only operation, and behaves conservatively before enough evidence exists. Machine-readable adaptive telemetry reports the learned thresholds and confidence used for each topology generation.

contracts.claim: Protocol-v4 peers exchange authenticated, cumulative endpoint capability snapshots and constrain physical-path work to their useful provider, cardinality, resource, and congestion intersection before optional lanes are launched.
contracts.assumption: Capabilities report bounded feature bits, provider candidate and ready counts, active-lane and session ceilings, endpoint CPU and memory ceilings, startup estimates, and current queue delay; they never report private identities or unauthenticated network input. The useful intersection takes the minimum cardinality and resource ceilings, the maximum bilateral startup and congestion costs, and only providers present at both endpoints. V1-v3 remain wire compatible and never receive the new frame. Capabilities are policy bounds and observations, not permission to weaken authenticated topology, minimum diversity, or local resource limits.
contracts.exit_condition: Locked wire vectors and malformed-input tests prove bounded canonical capability encoding. Authenticated v4 runtime tests prove cumulative replay after lane replacement, reject regression and conflicting same-generation content, and prove v3 compatibility without capability frames. Product tests prove that unavailable providers and excess candidate slots are excluded before supervisor startup, bilateral active/resource ceilings bound adaptive admission, and updated congestion/readiness snapshots alter the useful intersection without restarting the bond.

contracts.claim: Bulk chunk size adapts within fixed protocol bounds to measured path bandwidth-delay product and reorder pressure instead of imposing one static size on every anonymous path.
contracts.assumption: Typing and control chunking remains fixed. New bulk data uses the current smoothed lane rate and RTT, clamps the lane-specific bandwidth-delay proposal to the configured 16-64 KiB production range, halves it after one RTT of queued serialization, and uses the floor after two RTTs. Sparse selective acknowledgements and timeout retransmissions halve a session pressure ceiling; clean cumulative delivery restores it geometrically after eight ceiling-sized bytes. Frame, sender-window, and chunk-ledger limits remain authoritative; the scheduler allocates no decision scratch; retained chunks are never re-chunked.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic asymmetric-path tests prove BDP-driven growth, queue-delay and selective-acknowledgement reduction, clean-ack recovery, timeout backoff, exact reverse-order reassembly, immutable shared retransmission payloads, protected low-latency scheduling, fail-closed bounds, conservative chunk-ledger admission, and 16,384 adaptive decisions with zero heap-backed scheduler scratch. The paced-socket embedded proof hash-verifies fixed 32 KiB and adaptive 16-64 KiB transfers across two asymmetric lanes, keeps real-time data on the protected lane below 250 ms, retains at least 80 percent of independently measured aggregate capacity, and requires adaptive goodput to remain at least 90 percent of the fixed baseline. A public `BondedStream` regression drives a sustained application write through the same bridge used by SSH and proves high-BDP traffic reaches the 64 KiB scheduler ceiling instead of being fragmented by an 8 or 16 KiB adapter boundary; typing-sized writes retain protected scheduling.

contracts.claim: AnonSSH provides install, start, stop, status, and boot-restart behavior for the server and resident client broker without requiring users to compose process supervisors manually.
contracts.assumption: Linux user-systemd is the first service-manager backend. Install snapshots the effective non-secret product policy and absolute packaged launcher into user-scoped versioned state. Interactive unlock stores the explicitly entered password only in the mode-0600 runtime directory so crash restart works within that login but reboot returns to locked; unattended boot requires an explicitly selected owner-only regular credential file. AnonSSH never silently converts an interactive password into a persistent credential. Enabling a user unit means user-manager startup; pre-login machine boot additionally requires administrator-selected user lingering, which AnonSSH does not silently grant.
contracts.exit_condition: Packaged commands atomically install/update and remove broker/server user units, explicitly unlock or start them, stop all owned children, and report machine-readable installation, credential, unit, broker, dependency, and topology state. Generated units use a status-v7 resident broker, restart failures after two seconds, preserve persistent router roots, and condition server activation on credential readiness. Deterministic tests use isolated config/runtime directories and a fake service controller to prove owner-only files, symlink rejection, strict argument encoding, idempotent repeated install/start/stop/uninstall, locked startup rejection, runtime-secret cleanup, explicit persistent credential validation, and exact manager operations without touching the host manager. `make test-service-lifecycle` drives the wrapped package through that lifecycle and requires warning-free `systemd-analyze verify`; the existing packaged hard-crash campaign proves new broker/server processes reclaim endpoints and retained router state after forced exit.

contracts.claim: Multi-minute startup, fallback, admission, drain, and repair operations expose bounded human-readable provider progress instead of appearing hung, while explicit verbose output retains exact slot and route diagnostics.
contracts.assumption: Progress is structured state, not an unbounded log. Default terminal output summarizes meaningful provider-level changes and the selected route without internal phase names or JSON; verbose output remains redacted, bounded, and suitable for support evidence. Full state can also be queried from the broker or server lifecycle command.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests drive delayed, failed, retried, ready, draining, and repaired Tor and I2P slots; prove default summaries are deduplicated and understandable; and prove verbose mode retains ordered redacted slot attempts, deadlines, and the exact machine-readable automatic-route report. Packaged startup and recovery artifacts include final structured progress and causal failure without scraping human stderr.

contracts.claim: Users can select stable documented resource and transport profiles through a versioned configuration file while environment variables remain explicit test or emergency overrides.
contracts.assumption: Unknown keys, invalid versions, non-loopback managed endpoints, colliding roots, and unsafe resource limits fail closed. Built-in low, balanced, and performance profiles expand to complete validated settings and preserve deterministic defaults.
contracts.exit_condition: Parser and precedence tests cover absent, valid, unknown, malformed, migrated, and overridden configurations; doctor reports the effective redacted configuration; profile tests lock candidate limits, budgets, ramp policy, and state roots; packaged smoke uses the default file-free path.

contracts.claim: Automatic clients discover and authenticate whether a server offers mixed, Tor-only, or I2P-only bonding instead of requiring matching manual flags.
contracts.assumption: Topology offers are deterministically derivable or authenticated under the recovery bond key, cannot downgrade an explicitly required provider policy, and disclose no private identity material. Mixed, Tor-only, and I2P-only plans occupy disjoint lane-ID namespaces, so the existing authenticated first-lane join commits to one topology before session allocation. Manual topology selection remains authoritative.
contracts.exit_condition: Mixed, Tor-only, and I2P-only plans use disjoint lane-ID namespaces committed by the authenticated lane transcript; deterministic tests reject wrong descriptors, provider provenance, keys, oversized requests, and explicit-mode changes. `make live-auto-topology` connects auto mode to every server topology, removes the unrelated executable for homogeneous cases, and records the selected authenticated topology and active discovery lane through broker status v7.

contracts.claim: Automatic connection establishment races the preferred bond against delayed direct recovery candidates so a stalled provider cannot serialize every fallback deadline.
contracts.assumption: Bond remains preferred within a bounded head start, every candidate has an independent cancellation-safe deadline, only one successful OpenSSH route reaches the terminal, and losing routers and credentials are cleaned up.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic virtual-time tests cover fast bond, stalled bond with fast Tor, stalled Tor with I2P, simultaneous success, total failure, and cancellation cleanup. `make live-auto-fallback` stalls bond formation for two minutes, completes strict derived-key SSH over direct Tor in about twenty seconds, records candidate timing and cancellation, then stops the resident broker and all test-owned routers.

contracts.claim: Bond peers negotiate an authenticated supported protocol version and fail with an actionable compatibility result rather than relying on one immutable magic value.
contracts.assumption: Version masks and selection occupy the existing authenticated nonce fields, so the fixed v1 handshake length remains compatible with peers that treat those bytes as opaque. V2 binds the negotiated selection into its key schedule; V3 adds bounded monotonic join replay protection; V4 adds cumulative encrypted capability snapshots; V5 authenticates one nonzero server-process incarnation across every product lane so repair cannot splice a restarted peer into volatile session state; V6 reserves capability-gated symbolic service selection on every logical application stream while V1-v5 retain their raw-SSH application interpretation. V1 retains the original handshake, record, frame grammar, and key schedule. A caller that excludes V1 rejects a legacy peer. A caller that permits V1 deliberately permits an unmarked legacy response because no in-band protocol can distinguish an old peer from an authenticated peer emulating one; an advertised non-newest selection is rejected. Direct SSH recovery remains available across a bond incompatibility when both releases publish it.
contracts.exit_condition: Locked vectors and cross-version tests prove newest-common selection, authenticated v5-or-later server incarnation, both current/v5 downgrade directions, no-common-version failure, authenticated downgrade rejection, old-client/new-server and new-client/old-server behavior, unchanged v1 key and frame semantics, and rejection of mixed-version replacement lanes. The packaged embedded campaign transfers exact encrypted payloads through current/current, both current/frozen-v4 directions, both current/v3 and current/v2 directions, and both current/frozen-v1 directions, then records the complete compatibility matrix in the smoke artifact.

contracts.claim: After an AnonSSH broker or server process crash, a new process reclaims stale local control state, reuses persistent router state safely, and restores new connections without manual filesystem repair.
contracts.assumption: Existing SSH byte streams cannot survive loss of their owning process and are reported as terminated; restart recovery promises bounded reconnection, not impossible transparent continuation of in-memory protocol state. Linux-owned Tor, i2pd, and Dropbear children use kernel parent-death signaling in addition to destructor cleanup; the detached resident broker is excluded so it can outlive an invoking SSH client.
contracts.exit_condition: A deterministic subprocess test proves an owned child dies when its parent receives SIGKILL, including the fork-to-parent-death-signal race, and descendant accounting covers children launched by non-main worker threads. `make live-process-restart` SIGKILLs the broker and server during idle, startup, and active transfer; verifies stale-socket reclamation, managed endpoint release, retained router roots and destination, explicit old-stream failure, exact new SSH, bounded recovery timing, captured owned processes, and orphan-process count zero. The 2026-10-12 packaged artifact covered one-endpoint-at-a-time replacement, captured 22 processes, preserved the opposite endpoint, reconnected after server replacement in 12.248 seconds and broker replacement in 14.345 seconds, and left zero orphans.

contracts.claim: AnonSSH recovers new SSH connections after network roaming, suspend/resume, and one-endpoint-at-a-time process replacement without corrupting persistent identity or router state.
contracts.assumption: Monotonic runtime time deliberately ignores wall-clock correction. A large monotonic jump may expire a probe and replace a lane rather than trusting pre-suspend path state. Existing SSH byte streams are not durable protocol state and terminate when their owning broker or server is replaced or the aggregate bond has no active lane for thirty seconds; the promise is bounded exact reconnect while the opposite endpoint stays available, not terminal-session survival. Shorter total outages remain repairable. Repeated provider loss and temporary zero-lane loss model the transport-visible effects of roaming without requiring privileged host network mutation.
contracts.exit_condition: A deterministic paused-time test advances across a suspend-sized interval, proves that no unwritten probe expires, then proves a written unanswered probe fails its lane once without a retransmission storm. `make live-pool-recovery` proves exact delivery across repeated Tor, I2P, and temporary total path loss. `make live-process-restart` replaces the server while the broker remains live, then replaces the broker while the server remains live; each phase requires explicit old-stream termination, retained destination and router-root markers, exact new SSH, bounded recovery, endpoint reclamation, and zero orphan processes. Documentation states that wall-clock changes are irrelevant and transparent survival of an existing SSH stream is not promised.

contracts.claim: Release bootstrap data is reproducibly observed over time and selected for demonstrated identity longevity rather than rotated by a short release-time freshness window.
contracts.assumption: Only signed public RouterInfos currently corroborated by configured mature sources may ship; private keys and profiles remain excluded. A long-lived identity still needs a recent signed RouterInfo to be immediately useful because addresses and RouterInfo timestamps change. Old embedded records remain disposable hints and ordinary verified reseed remains available, but package publication is not blocked merely because a fixed number of hours elapsed after curation.
contracts.exit_condition: Make targets separately report the current ledger without mutation, inspect current source-root contribution without recording an observation, collect a deterministic daily observation into that versioned ledger, stage the uncapped qualifying corpus, review its complete diff, promote it, and validate manifest integrity. The ledger report includes the observation-day distribution, maximum observed span, earliest possible span completion, and number of identities whose history meets policy. The source report reuses the curator's positive-evidence and 24-hour recency rules, reports each root's usable identity count and newest evidence ages, and fails when the configured roots cannot currently corroborate any candidate. Validation reports observation-span and RouterInfo-age distributions without imposing the former 24-hour release deadline. Package and gate builds validate longevity evidence and digests. The first real two-source observation is retained even when no new identity can honestly satisfy seven days yet, and subsequent observations can promote qualifying identities without forgetting temporarily absent routers. Documentation distinguishes identity longevity, current RouterInfo usefulness, and certificate-verified reseed fallback.

contracts.claim: A NixOS repository can package AnonSSH with its own pinned nixpkgs through pkgs.callPackage without copying runtime dependency paths or using AnonSSH's fallback nixpkgs pin.
contracts.assumption: The consuming repository pins the complete reviewed AnonSSH source tree, including Cargo.lock and bootstrap data. AnonSSH remains one package expression rather than owning a second NixOS module; its packaged CLI continues to own the per-user service lifecycle.
contracts.exit_condition: A normal Make target resolves the caller's explicit nixpkgs path, builds default.nix through that package set's callPackage, executes the resulting wrapped binary's version and JSON doctor commands, and records machine-readable artifacts. The target is part of make gate, and documentation gives the minimal NixOS package binding without prescribing mutable checkout paths.

contracts.claim: A NixOS host can build the same AnonSSH Rust product without embedding Tor, i2pd, OpenSSH, or Dropbear executable payloads, while the Nix closure supplies exact runtime programs and the complete adaptive networking behavior remains available.
contracts.assumption: This is a source-built personal integration product rather than a portable artifact or a protocol fork. Its executable retains the public I2P bootstrap corpus and i2pd certificate path, but depends on its Nix store closure and therefore must not be copied out of that closure as a standalone binary. The portable static release continues to embed all six executable payloads and remains unchanged.
contracts.exit_condition: A stable nix/monsternix.nix entry point requires the caller's pkgs, disables all compile-time executable payloads, and wraps the resulting anonssh with caller-selected Tor, i2pd, OpenSSH, Dropbear, certificate, and bootstrap paths. A normal Make target builds through an explicit caller nixpkgs, runs version, deterministic self-test, and JSON doctor in an isolated cache, proves that all six embedded-version fields are null, proves every runtime dependency resolves inside /nix/store, proves no embedded runtime cache is created, and writes a versioned machine-readable report under artifacts/. The target is part of make gate and documentation provides a direct configuration.nix package expression.

contracts.claim: The portable AnonSSH executable contains pinned static Tor and i2pd router executables plus i2pd certificate material, while explicit operator overrides remain authoritative.
contracts.assumption: The upstream routers remain separate executables launched as managed child processes; embedding is distribution aggregation, not source-level linking. Runtime payloads are extracted only into a private per-user content-addressed cache, validated before every use, and never accepted from a symlink or mismatched file. ANONSSH_TOR_BIN, ANONSSH_I2PD_BIN, and ANONSSH_I2PD_CERTS_DIR deliberately select operator-managed alternatives. Reusing an already-running external i2pd SAM service is supported by the managed endpoint contract; attaching to an arbitrary external Tor service requires authenticated control ownership and is not implied by executable override.
contracts.exit_condition: The Nix package builds the pinned latest reviewed Tor and i2pd releases as static Linux executables and feeds them plus certificates into the Rust build. Deterministic tests prove explicit override precedence, exact content-addressed extraction, owner-only executable modes, certificate extraction, idempotent reuse, corruption rejection, and absent-payload fallback. The static release has no ELF interpreter or dynamic dependencies, reports both embedded router versions, and passes doctor with router variables unset and a PATH containing no Tor or i2pd. Distribution documentation carries upstream version, license, and corresponding-source obligations.

contracts.claim: An operator may explicitly attach an AnonSSH Tor slot to an already-running local Tor service without granting AnonSSH process ownership or weakening control authentication.
contracts.assumption: An occupied endpoint is never adopted implicitly. Each configuration-v2 external service record binds one exact non-zero loopback SOCKS endpoint to one exact loopback control endpoint and an owner-only regular 32-byte CookieAuthentication file. The operator configures IsolateSOCKSAuth; AnonSSH authenticates the control endpoint and verifies bootstrap before use, never stops the external process, and treats loss of authenticated health as a lane failure. Distinct declared services remain distinct failure domains; repeating one control cookie under several slots is rejected rather than misrepresented as independent-path evidence.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests reject undeclared, partial, non-loopback, duplicate, malformed-cookie, symlink, and unauthenticated occupied endpoints; accept an exactly declared authenticated service; return no owned-process resource usage; preserve it across AnonSSH stop/drop; and fail after authenticated health disappears. Service installation freezes validated declarations into the owner-only product config without systemd environment drop-ins. Documentation defines the stable v2 record and distinguishes an external daemon from an external executable override.

contracts.claim: AnonSSH produces one statically linked Linux executable that runs on NixOS and conventional Linux distributions without a Nix runtime or adjacent bootstrap files.
contracts.assumption: Tor, i2pd, OpenSSH, and Dropbear remain independent managed child executables but are carried as static payloads in the portable artifact; explicit environment overrides can select external copies. The public I2P corpus and public router runtime material are safe to embed, while router profiles and every private identity remain excluded.
contracts.exit_condition: The sole Nix expression builds an unwrapped musl executable; a normal Make target rejects any ELF interpreter or NEEDED entry in the outer executable and every embedded program, runs version, embedded deterministic tests, a real local SSH login, and doctor with an empty PATH, and records a machine-readable release report. With no corpus environment variable, runtime validation and fresh-state import use the same digest-checked corpus embedded at compile time. The full gate builds this artifact, and first-use documentation names the embedded programs, exact client command, password and machine-ID requirements, cold-start expectations, and server unlock behavior.

contracts.claim: A downloaded AnonSSH executable contains every program required for client and server operation and is accompanied by architecture-explicit integrity, provenance, license, and corresponding-source metadata.
contracts.assumption: Six executable payloads from four independently licensed upstream projects (Tor, i2pd, OpenSSH ssh/scp/sftp-server, and Dropbear) are embedded as exact static bytes rather than linked into Rust. Tor is separately linked against the selected static libevent, OpenSSL, zlib, xz, zstd, and scrypt inputs, and reseed certificates come from the Java I2P package rather than i2pd; all seven origins are release components even though they are not executable payloads. Explicit executable overrides remain authoritative. Reproducibility means two isolated builds from the same reviewed source and pinned Nix inputs produce the same executable digest. Nix cargoDeps and some upstream trees are symlink farms whose links may target the build machine's store; a corresponding-source archive is complete only after every input is materialized as ordinary directories and files with no surviving symlink. A repository-generated unsigned checksum is integrity metadata, not publisher authentication; release signing requires an external publisher-controlled private key. The supported portable release target is x86-64 Linux; AArch64 is deliberately outside the current product contract.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic tests cover content-addressed extraction, exact digest and mode validation, corruption and symlink rejection, and explicit override precedence for all six executable payloads. `make package-static` resolves no runtime dependency through PATH, proves the outer binary and all six extracted programs have no ELF interpreter or NEEDED entry, runs an embedded client/server SSH, SFTP-subsystem, and legacy-scp-helper proof, emits a versioned release manifest, SHA-256 checksum file, SPDX SBOM, license inventory, and corresponding-source inventory covering every executable payload, all six selected Tor link inputs, and the Java I2P certificate source, and rejects a corresponding-source archive containing any symlink or missing named source. The source derivation follows each input link while copying, requires every vendored Rust dependency to contain Cargo.toml, fails if a link remains before archiving, and records materialized file and dependency counts. Publication extraction independently repeats the zero-link check. `make package-static-reproducible` builds twice through independent output paths and requires identical digests. A detached signature is accepted only from an explicitly supplied publisher key and its verification result is recorded without silently generating a release identity.

contracts.claim: The primary recovery interface is `anonssh user@machine-id`, which immediately follows the existing connect path and requests the shared identity password.
contracts.assumption: Only one bare argument containing `@` is shorthand; explicit subcommands and their options retain the established grammar, and the existing strict recovery-target parser remains authoritative. The downloadable x86-64 Linux artifact is named `anonssh`; architecture and linkage remain explicit in its release report.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic parser tests prove the bare target becomes the exact Connect command, malformed target syntax reaches the same fail-closed validation, and named commands are unchanged. The static package target emits `artifacts/release/anonssh`, captures and asserts its generated direct-form help, and documentation leads with the direct command while retaining `anonssh connect` as the explicit advanced form.

contracts.claim: An authenticated user can expose one explicitly named remote TCP service on a loopback-only local TCP listener over the same automatic, Tor-only, I2P-only, or mixed bonded recovery path used by SSH.
contracts.assumption: The adapter is implemented as hardened OpenSSH local forwarding so existing SSH server authorization remains authoritative. The local endpoint must be a nonzero loopback socket, the remote host and nonzero port must pass strict bounded parsing, route/identity/trust options remain non-overridable, and forwarding failure must terminate the command rather than silently leave a partial listener. This is not an arbitrary unauthenticated exit proxy. Unix-socket forwarding requires a separate stale-path and ownership contract.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic parser and command-vector tests reject wildcard, unspecified, multicast, malformed, zero-port, control-character, option-like, and ambiguous unbracketed IPv6 inputs while preserving bracketed IPv6 and DNS names. A packaged live mixed-bond test starts a named TCP echo service behind the recovery server, invokes `anonssh forward`, exchanges exact independently hashed payloads in both directions through the local listener, observes the bonded path, and proves child, router, socket, and test-state cleanup.

contracts.claim: Rust applications can construct and operate a bonded transport through high-level `BondDialer` and `BondListener` provider interfaces without manually assembling authenticated runtime lanes.
contracts.assumption: Provider policy, endpoint authorization, lifecycle ownership, progress, and resource limits are explicit traits or configuration; the API cannot become an unauthenticated open proxy and keeps the runtime-independent core separate from Tokio/provider integration. A dial provider receives the complete prepared authenticated client hello as initial transport payload before `BondDialer` waits for the server response. Ordinary stream providers write and flush that payload immediately after connection, while I2P injects it into the SAM STREAM CONNECT operation because an inbound I2P stream may not become acceptable before initial data exists. Tor and I2P provider adapters own anonymous-network stream dialing and publication, while router process supervision, persistent state, warming, and machine-wide resource allocation remain application policy.
contracts.exit_condition: The public documented API and external-crate test bind three race-free ephemeral loopback endpoints, form a two-lane random-epoch session, require one nonzero listener incarnation across initial and dynamic current-version ABP handshakes, open exact interactive and bulk streams, authenticate and add a third lane, replace that lane over the retained listener, observe live and snapshotted structured progress, and shut down both sessions and the listener cleanly. Its dial provider rejects the old plain-dial path and requires `BondDialer` to supply a valid ABP client hello through the atomic initial-payload operation. The same deterministic suite compiles a custom object-safe provider that implements only the compatible plain-dial method, rejects non-loopback and non-allowlisted endpoints and actions, drops cancelled operations, and measures the configured two-operation parallel ceiling. Public Tor SOCKS/onion-control and I2P SAM dial/listen adapters require numeric loopback router endpoints and exact listener bindings, redact private material, and pass external black-box wire tests for outbound and inbound bytes, endpoint denial, SOCKS destination selection, Tor control authentication and keyed publication, and SAM session creation. A paired fake-SAM proof withholds connection success until it receives the prepared ABP hello, bridges the resulting streams, forms a mutually authenticated high-level `BondDialer`/`BondListener` session through the public I2P providers, exchanges an exact encrypted `BondedStream` payload, and shuts down cleanly.

contracts.claim: The shipped AnonSSH binary can deterministically stress every security-relevant bond and I2P bootstrap parser with bounded malformed and valid-roundtrip inputs without relying on an external fuzzing toolchain.
contracts.assumption: A fixed-seed mutation campaign is a reproducible gate and regression corpus rather than open-ended coverage-guided fuzzing. Inputs and iteration counts remain explicitly bounded so attacker-controlled length fields cannot turn the self-test into unbounded allocation or runtime. Authenticated wire structures are tested both before authentication and after recomputing valid authentication over structurally malformed fields so validation below the MAC boundary is exercised.
contracts.exit_condition: `anonssh test --fuzz --json` runs fixed-seed campaigns over ABP frame, acknowledgement, stream-control, capability, topology, lane-handshake, encrypted-record, I2P manifest, observation-ledger, and peer-profile parsers; checks canonical round trips for accepted values; and emits a versioned machine-readable report with nonzero accepted and rejected coverage for every applicable family. `make test-fuzz` writes that report under artifacts, the target is part of `make gate`, and static package smoke runs the same facility from the shipped binary with no external runtime dependency. Any panic, timeout, noncanonical acceptance, violated bound, or parser invariant fails closed.

contracts.claim: Typing-sized bond data can trade bounded duplicate bytes for lower tail latency by racing the two protected paths while preserving one ordered, exactly-once logical stream.
contracts.assumption: Only explicitly enabled Realtime data and Interactive chunks at or below 2 KiB are eligible; control and bulk remain single-copy. One primary and at most one distinct active protected lane carry the same authenticated stream offset and shared immutable payload, so existing reassembly accepts the first copy and eliminates the second. Sender credit and retained payload are charged once. A full or closed shadow queue drops only the redundant copy and cannot turn an accepted primary dispatch into application failure. Winner-attributed replication is enabled only under negotiated ABP v3 because legacy peers may route acknowledgements over unrelated lanes; immediate v3 acknowledgements return on the winning ingress lane when possible so path measurements do not systematically credit a stalled primary. When two protected slots and healthy Tor and I2P lanes are available, one slot from each provider limits correlated overlay failure; unique router failure domains remain separate and homogeneous bonds retain their two best independent lanes. This reduces transport jitter but cannot provide Mosh-style zero-RTT predictive echo because the current adapter intentionally sees only encrypted OpenSSH bytes and owns no terminal screen model. Retained sub-second quiet measurements are an empirical operating envelope, not an SLA. Bond work optimizes actual delivery consistency, contention isolation, and pathological tails; LAN-like perceived typing requires a separately specified terminal layer and is not a transport completion criterion.
contracts.exit_condition: Deterministic scheduler and sender tests prove allocation-free selection of two distinct protected lanes, mixed-provider protection when both providers are healthy, late restoration of missing provider protection, unchanged two-lane homogeneous protection, one offset and payload allocation, one sender-window charge, alternate-winner acknowledgement attribution, exact first-copy delivery, duplicate elimination, no bulk replication, and single-lane degradation. Runtime tests stall the preferred writer and deliver typing through the protected standby before failure detection, then saturate a blocked shadow queue while primary delivery remains exact and reports bounded redundancy drops. Endurance evidence records redundant and dropped real-time frame deltas. Quiet evidence uses fixed-cadence request/echo samples over one persistent Realtime stream and keeps its aggregate separate from legacy one-way/lifecycle samples; loaded legacy history is preserved without relabeling. A retained public-overlay run must compare valid echoed typing tails and show both-provider winners before this contract is promoted.

contracts.claim: Programs that accept an SSH-compatible remote-shell executable can invoke AnonSSH directly while retaining the password-plus-machine-ID trust and routing model.
contracts.assumption: Compatibility means a documented fail-closed subset of the OpenSSH command-line and process contract, not acceptance of every ssh option. AnonSSH consumes user and machine identity itself, preserves route, key, and host-trust policy, passes the remote command to embedded OpenSSH without re-tokenizing it, keeps progress on stderr, never reads protocol stdin for a password, and returns the remote command's exit status. Remote executables remain destination dependencies unless separately embedded. Stock rsync, Git, Borg, scp, SFTP, and SSHFS clients select AnonSSH through their standard SSH hooks; no tool-specific AnonSSH subcommand or protocol adapter is added. The release embeds the OpenSSH SFTP subsystem and legacy scp server helper, and managed Dropbear receives only their validated content-addressed paths. SSHFS remains dependent on local FUSE support, and Borg remains dependent on a compatible destination executable.
contracts.exit_condition: The invocation parser accepts both `anonssh user@machine [command ...]` and remote-shell generated `anonssh -l user machine [command ...]`, separates pre-destination options from post-destination command arguments, supports `--`, and rejects route, identity, trust, port, configuration, command-injection, and proxy overrides. Exact disabling values and harmless flags emitted by proven stock clients are accepted without admitting enabling or route-changing forms. The SSH adapter preserves operating-system command arguments and OpenSSH remote-shell semantics, obtains the identity password outside protocol stdin, emits no AnonSSH data on stdout, propagates remote exit status, and retains interactive PTY behavior when no command is supplied. Deterministic tests cover generated argument forms, option-like commands, spaces, safe and protected options, exact command placement, helper extraction and routing, and status conversion. The packaged `make live-bond-tools` campaign proves bidirectional rsync with metadata and resume; Git push/clone/fetch; Borg repository initialization, archive creation, repository check, and exact extraction; default SFTP-based scp, direct SFTP, and legacy scp upload/download; SSHFS exact read/write, rename, and managed unmount; exact stdout/stderr; remote exit 23; clean missing-command failure; and independent SSH streams over one reused bond session.

contracts.claim: Local applications can dial explicitly named peer services through the adaptive bond over an owner-only versioned Unix socket without implementing ABP, SSH, Tor, or I2P.
contracts.assumption: ALP1 uses a public application socket distinct from the broker's privileged internal control socket and never accepts arbitrary Tor/I2P destinations, raw bond keys, remote TCP addresses, or filesystem paths supplied by a peer. One local connection maps to one independent BondedStream and becomes a raw full-duplex byte stream only after a bounded framed setup exchange succeeds. Targets must already be authorized into a bounded in-memory broker registry by the controlling-terminal password flow; authorizations expire on broker exit or after twelve idle hours. The mode-0600 public listener verifies Linux peer UID, shares the private runtime directory and broker lease, and uses the resident connection limit. ABP v6 carries the authenticated capability-negotiated ASP1 stream-service preface, reserved built-in `ssh` service, and startup-configured symbolic registry whose owner-private Unix socket is revalidated before every connection and limited to sixteen streams. `anonssh dial` is the stdio client. This is not Unix-domain-socket forwarding, SOCKS, TUN, or an arbitrary network exit.
contracts.exit_condition: The documented `ALP1` protocol uses bounded length-prefixed setup/result records followed by an unframed raw stream after exactly one ready result. The listener lives below an owner-only runtime directory, creates a mode-0600 socket without following symlinks, verifies Linux peer credentials, bounds setup time, record size, connections, and per-service concurrency, and rejects stale or mismatched target authorization. Authenticated peers negotiate service multiplexing before a stream is exposed; each stream carries a bounded symbolic service name and existing ABP traffic class, receives an explicit accept or rejection, and can reach only a locally configured owner-private Unix socket. Deterministic tests cover strict framing, downgrade, unauthorized UID, stale and unsafe paths, registry expiry, service denial, class policy, exact half-close, and open-proxy shapes. The packaged `make live-bond-native` campaign hash-verifies concurrent bulk and real-time native echo streams over real Tor and I2P, requires independent stream IDs on one reused mixed bond session, verifies owner-only ALP socket modes, and succeeds only after process, endpoint, socket, and test-state cleanup.

contracts.claim: Applications can dynamically publish native services and consume ALP through maintained connected-stream Rust, C, Python, and Go clients with equivalent behavior across mixed and homogeneous bonds.
contracts.assumption: Dynamic publication requires a same-UID lease and exact local path/class/concurrency policy; it must not broaden ALP into arbitrary forwarding. Richer setup progress must remain bounded and versioned. The mixed static-service proof does not establish Tor-only, I2P-only, concurrent SSH/native isolation, churn, restart, or language-binding conformance.
contracts.exit_condition: A separate owner-only registration endpoint supports bounded same-UID leases, revalidates every Unix socket, denies stale registrations, and drains or resets streams according to documented policy. Packaged mixed, Tor-only, and I2P-only campaigns hash-verify simultaneous SSH, bulk native, and real-time native traffic, prove independent stream isolation and adaptive lane contribution through churn and restart, and leave no residue. Rust, C, Python, and Go clients pass shared black-box fixtures for strict setup records, progress, ready transition, structured errors, deadlines, half-close, cancellation, and reconnect without exposing ABP credentials or provider endpoints.
